summary: The Stop hook. .claude/hooks/require-verdict.sh blocks a session that tries to end an autonomous iteration without a verdict artifact, and every block hands the agent state-changing moves rather than just a refusal. Bounded at 2 blocks per iteration via a counter cleanup_artifacts clears; inert outside the loop and on the happy path; never satisfied by an artifact left from an earlier iteration. The verdict vocabulary is defined once in run-until-done.sh and exported, so the hook and the dispatcher cannot disagree about what an ending is. Also ships item 5 (prompt guidance) and — beyond the literal kickoff — an additive hook-registration sync in enrich-project.py without which the hook would never fire in any existing project.
suggested_commit_message: session lifetime: Stop hook — a session may not end without a verdict
reviewer_notes: Audit first: no Stop hook existed; PreToolUse (deny-dangerous-commands) and SessionStart (compact-reanchor) are the established patterns and this follows them.

The vocabulary is exported by the loop (PHASEKIT_VERDICT_ARTIFACTS) rather than restated in the hook, and a test asserts the hook does NOT contain the artifact names. Kickoff said to enumerate from the loop; exporting is how that becomes structural instead of a convention.

Freshness uses the loop's existing ITER_START_MARKER, exported as PHASEKIT_ITER_MARKER, so the hook answers 'written this iteration?' with the same mechanism as artifact_written_this_iteration(). No second mechanism was invented.

Inert outside the loop is a deliberate fourth property beyond the kickoff's three: the hook needs all three PHASEKIT_* vars to have any opinion, so an interactive `claude` session can never be blocked. Blocking one would violate phasekit's standing rule that ordinary direct work must not be made cumbersome.
Fail-open everywhere except the deliberate block, including an unwritable artifacts dir: cannot count means cannot bound, which means it must not block.

ADDITION BEYOND THE KICKOFF, flagged for Aaron. The kickoff assumed registering the file in capabilities was enough. It is not: .claude/settings.json is bootstrap-with-template-tracking (write-once), so an upgrade installs the hook FILE and never the Stop REGISTRATION. Verified empirically before writing any code — a project enriched pre-release then upgraded had the script on disk and no Stop entry. Shipping that way would have delivered a believed no-op to all 8 fleet projects, including the one the incident happened in. sync_hook_registrations() closes it: additive only, driven by the settings template (already the single source of truth for the wiring), idempotent, never touching permissions/env/project-owned hooks.

Mutation-testing protocol as an opt-in capability profile (kickoff item 4), docs, release.
